text.p: - Representatives of the five successor states of the former Yugoslavia, meeting in Brussels, failed to agree on a division of assets of the former federation.
- Slovenian President Milan Kucan, on a six-day visit to China, met his Chinese counterpart Jiang Zemin on Monday.

- A Paris court on Monday temporarily blocked banks Credit Lyonnais and Societe General to transfer funds of the former National Bank of Yugoslavia to the Banque Franco-Yugoslave. The court will hold its next hearing in the case on December 11.
- Slovenian unions have not yet decided how to respond to employers' calls for cuts in work benefits.
- The president of the council for Slovenia's National Cultural Programme resigned, claiming the ministry of culture exerted too much control over cultural policy.

- Electronic components maker Elektronika, which used to be a part of Gorenje Elektronika group that went bankrupt in 1993, has returned to the black after completing a restructuring programme administered by the state-owned Development Fund.
- Yugoslav customs officers on Sunday discovered 190 kg of heroin in a Slovenian truck.
- Production at paper factory Videm, halted earlier this month after the hand-over of the company to its Czech buyer ICEC, has not yet restarted.
